description: The Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Mathematics at Kent State University provides students with a strong foundation in mathematics, statistics, and finance, essential for a career as an actuary. The curriculum covers topics such as probability, statistics, financial mathematics, economics, and actuarial models, preparing students for the preliminary exams of the Society of Actuaries (SOA) and the Casualty Actuarial Society (CAS). The program emphasizes practical skills through courses in statistical software and real-world applications. Graduates are well-prepared for entry-level positions in insurance companies, consulting firms, government agencies, and other organizations requiring actuarial expertise. Additionally, the program prepares students for graduate studies in actuarial science or related quantitative fields. Our dedicated faculty members, many of whom are credentialed actuaries, provide individualized attention and mentorship, helping students achieve their academic and professional goals.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Mathematics

description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in Africana Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a comprehensive understanding of Africana peoples and cultures in Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America and the United States. The program exposes students to critical thinking, reading and writing in several academic areas (humanities, social sciences and the arts). Africana Studies helps students to connect historical and contemporary issues; to develop a global perspective; and to appreciate cultural diversity. The program provides the necessary knowledge and skills for graduates to succeed in the 21st century.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Africana Studies

description: The Air Traffic and Airspace Management B.S. degree provides students with a strong foundation in aviation management, air traffic control and flight operations. Graduates of this program will be prepared for a career as an air traffic controller, or other careers in aviation management and flight operations. The Air Traffic and Airspace Management program is approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) under Title 14 CFR Part 65 for air traffic control training. Graduates of this program will receive a letter of accomplishment that may reduce the length of air traffic control training at the FAA Academy in Oklahoma City.
Accreditation status: Approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) under Title 14 CFR Part 65 for air traffic control training.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Air Traffic and Airspace Management

description: The Bachelor of Arts in American Sign Language (ASL) is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a thorough grounding in ASL linguistics, deaf culture and the history of the deaf community. The program is designed to provide students with the linguistic and cultural competency necessary for success in careers that involve working with deaf individuals and the deaf community, as well as prepare them for further graduate study in ASL linguistics, deaf studies, interpreting and other related fields. Students will develop proficiency in ASL and learn about various aspects of deaf culture, including its history, values, and social norms. Students will also gain an understanding of the linguistic features of ASL, including its phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. The program offers opportunities for experiential learning through interaction with the deaf community and service-learning projects. Overall, the BA in ASL program aims to equip students with the knowledge, skills, and cultural awareness necessary to become effective communicators and advocates for the deaf community.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in American Sign Language

description:
The Bachelor of Science degree in American Sign Language/English Interpreting prepares students for professional careers as interpreters in a wide range of settings, including educational, legal, medical, mental health, business, employment and video relay services.
This program develops fluency in American Sign Language and spoken English, as well as an understanding of the cultural characteristics of both the Deaf and hearing communities. Students also learn interpreting theory, ethics and professional standards and develop the interpreting skills necessary to work between these two languages and cultures. Graduates of the program are well-prepared to take the national certification examination for interpreters.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in American Sign Language/English Interpreting

description: The Animation Game Design (AGD) B.S. degree is for students interested in a career in the interactive entertainment industry focusing on the artistic and aesthetic elements of games, or in the fields of animation, interactive media and simulation. The AGD curriculum allows students to develop the aesthetic and technical skills needed to create engaging and impactful games, interactive experiences and animations. Graduates with the AGD degree find careers in the gaming industry as designers, artists, animators and producers. In addition, the AGD degree prepares students for careers in 3D animation, interactive media, simulation, architectural visualization and other visual effects related fields. Graduates also pursue graduate school to further their education.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Animation Game Design

description: The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) degree in Anthropology is designed for students seeking a broad education in the discipline to develop skills in critical thinking, writing, problem-solving, cultural competency and data analysis relevant to a variety of careers. The Anthropology B.A. provides students with a foundational understanding of the four subfields of anthropology: cultural anthropology, archaeology, biological anthropology and linguistic anthropology. Students gain an understanding of humanity from a holistic and cross-cultural perspective and learn to apply theoretical and methodological approaches to human behavior, societies, cultures and their origins. The B.A. program provides flexibility to allow students to pair anthropology with another major or a minor to prepare for a wide variety of career opportunities, including education, government, museum work, international business, social services and non-governmental organizations, public health, law and policy, scientific research, forensic science and cultural resource management. Students can also pursue further study in graduate school in any of the four subfields of anthropology and related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology

description: The Bachelor of Science in Anthropology degree is designed for students who want a strong grounding in the natural sciences in addition to an understanding of human culture and society. Students pursuing the B.S. in Anthropology will conduct field and laboratory research to better understand human origins, evolution, and variation. While the program’s focus is on science, students also will be introduced to social and cultural anthropology. The B.S. degree is excellent preparation for graduate studies in biological anthropology and archaeology or careers in forensic anthropology, museum studies, public health, law, and medicine.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Anthropology

description: The Bachelor of Business Administration (B.B.A.) in Accounting program focuses on financial, managerial, governmental and international accounting, auditing and taxation. The program develops critical skills for accounting professionals and prepares students for a variety of entry-level professional positions and graduate studies in accounting, business, law and other fields. The B.B.A. in Accounting curriculum is designed to provide students with the necessary foundation to pass professional examinations such as the Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Certified Management Accountant (CMA), Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) and others. Students considering a career in public accounting should carefully review the education requirements for CPA licensure in the state where they plan to practice. For Ohio, students must complete 150 semester hours of education to sit for the CPA exam and 150 semester hours of education for licensure. The B.B.A. in Accounting program requires 120 semester hours; therefore, students seeking CPA licensure must pursue additional hours of education beyond the B.B.A. in Accounting degree.
Program name: Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting

description: If you enjoy working with numbers and wish to start your career quickly, a two-year associate degree in Accounting Technology may be for you. Accountants play a key role in the success of every business, making accounting a stable and in-demand profession. Through Kent State's Accounting Technology associate degree, you will gain the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue a variety of accounting support positions in industry, small business, public accounting, and government. These include positions such as: Accounts Payable Clerk, Accounts Receivable Clerk, Bookkeeper, Payroll Clerk, Staff Accountant and Tax Preparer. Your studies will cover principles of financial and managerial accounting, computerized accounting applications and income tax preparation. Additionally, the program includes a capstone experience where you’ll demonstrate the skills learned by engaging in a simulated business situation using current accounting software.
Program name: Associate of Applied Business in Accounting Technology

description:
The Aeronautical Studies B.S. degree program at Kent State University provides students with a broad and comprehensive understanding of the aviation industry, preparing them for diverse careers in aviation operations, management, safety, and more. This program is designed for students passionate about aviation who seek a strong foundational knowledge without pursuing a pilot or air traffic control certification.

Students in the Aeronautical Studies B.S. program will develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and leadership skills essential for success in the dynamic aviation industry. The curriculum covers key areas such as aviation history, aviation law, airport operations, airline management, aviation safety, human factors in aviation, and current issues in aviation. Graduates are well-prepared for roles in airline operations, airport management, aviation consulting, regulatory compliance, aviation safety analysis, and other non-flying aviation professions.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Studies

description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Aeronautical Systems Engineering Technology at Kent State University prepares students for a variety of technical and leadership careers in the aeronautical industry. The curriculum provides students with a strong foundation in science, mathematics, computer applications and communication. Students are introduced to the core concepts of aeronautical engineering technology, including aircraft systems, aviation safety, air transportation, air traffic control and unmanned aircraft systems. The program emphasizes hands-on learning through laboratory experiences, projects and internships. Graduates are prepared for careers in areas such as aircraft design and manufacturing, maintenance, operations, air traffic management, aviation safety, airport management and unmanned aircraft systems.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Systems Engineering Technology

description: The Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering program provides students with a strong foundation in the principles of aerospace design, analysis and testing. Students gain knowledge and skills in aerodynamics, propulsion, flight mechanics, structural analysis and control systems. The program prepares graduates for careers in the aerospace industry, government agencies and further graduate studies. Through a rigorous curriculum and hands-on projects, students develop critical thinking, problem-solving skills and the ability to contribute to the advancement of aerospace technology.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering

description:
The Bachelor of Science in Advertising degree program prepares students for careers in the dynamic and creative world of advertising. Students learn how to conceive, produce, and manage advertising campaigns across various media platforms. The program emphasizes strategic thinking, creative problem-solving, and practical application of advertising principles. Graduates are equipped with the skills needed to succeed in advertising agencies, media companies, corporate marketing departments, and entrepreneurial ventures.
Through this program, students will learn to:
* Identify and understand target audiences and consumer behavior.
* Develop effective advertising strategies and integrated marketing communications plans.
* Create compelling advertising messages and content for various media.
* Utilize research and data analytics to inform advertising decisions.
* Manage advertising campaigns from concept to execution.
* Understand the ethical and legal responsibilities in advertising.
* Collaborate effectively in team environments to produce advertising solutions.
Accreditation status: The School of Media and Journalism is accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC).
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Advertising

description: The Minor in Accessories provides students with foundational design and technical skills related to product development in fashion accessories including handbags, footwear and small leather goods. Students learn design, pattern making, construction and manufacturing processes for accessories that culminate in a collection of accessory products. This minor is open to all students, regardless of their major.
Program name: Minor in Accessories

description: The Minor in Accounting program provides non-accounting majors with an understanding of accounting systems and processes. It introduces students to financial and managerial accounting concepts, as well as accounting information systems and taxation. The minor provides foundational knowledge relevant to any business career.
Accreditation status: All undergraduate and graduate programs within the Ambassador Crawford College of Business and Entrepreneurship are accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.
Program name: Minor in Accounting

description: This minor is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the principles and practices of audio recording and production. Students will gain hands-on experience with industry-standard equipment and software, covering topics such as acoustics, microphone techniques, mixing, mastering, and live sound reinforcement. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical knowledge and practical application, preparing students for entry-level positions in audio production, sound engineering, and related fields, or for further studies in audio arts.
Accreditation status: The Hugh A. Glauser School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).
Program name: Minor in Music in Audio Recording

description: The Dance Studies B.A. program provides students with a broad and inclusive view of dance within a liberal arts curriculum. With an emphasis on critical thinking and theoretical understanding, students explore topics such as dance history, aesthetics, criticism, cultural contexts, pedagogy, anatomy/kinesiology, music for dance, and creative processes. The program prepares students for various career paths in the field of dance, including arts administration, dance education, dance writing/criticism, dance research, and other related fields. Our graduates are equipped to pursue further studies at the graduate level, enriching their knowledge and developing specialized skills.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD)
Program name: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Dance

description: The Minor in Dance provides an overview of dance as a performing art form with a strong emphasis in contemporary dance. Students in the minor develop skills in technical training, creative processes, historical/cultural contexts and somatic practices. The minor may be pursued by students in any major, complementing a variety of interests. The curriculum promotes critical thinking, communication, creative problem-solving and collaboration skills while cultivating an appreciation for the artistic discipline of dance.
Program name: Minor in Dance

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Dance Studies degree is intended for students who wish to pursue a career in dance education (K-12 licensure), dance history, dance criticism, or dance administration. This flexible curriculum allows students to pursue coursework in other fields while developing strong dance technique and a broad understanding of dance as an art form.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Dance Studies

description: Kent State's Bachelor of Fine Arts (B.F.A.) in Musical Theatre provides comprehensive training in acting, singing and dancing, with equal emphasis on each area. Students are prepared for a career in musical theatre and can expect to gain invaluable experience on stage in multiple productions, including those produced by Porthouse Theatre, the department’s professional summer theatre. The School of Theatre and Dance maintains an extremely active production schedule providing students with a wealth of opportunities to perform. The B.F.A. in Musical Theatre is a rigorous program that requires an audition and interview for acceptance. Musical Theatre students take classes in acting, stage movement, ballet, jazz, tap, music theory, voice, musical theatre history, and private voice.
Program name: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Musical Theatre

description:
The Bachelor of Fine Arts (B.F.A.) degree in Theatre Design, Technology and Production is a highly specialized, pre-professional degree for students with demonstrated aptitude and interest in a career in theatre design and technology. This rigorous professional program offers extensive practical experience and training to prepare students for careers in the professional, educational, and entertainment industries. Through production experience, internships, and faculty mentorship, students gain real-world experience and develop skills and knowledge in all areas of theatrical design, technology, and production management.
The B.F.A. curriculum balances intensive classroom and studio instruction with a commitment to providing quality production opportunities through the School of Theatre and Dance’s annual production season. Areas of study include scenic, costume, lighting, and sound design; technical direction; stage management; properties; stagecraft; costume technology; theatrical rigging; digital media; and theatrical drafting.
Accreditation status: Kent State University’s School of Theatre and Dance is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).
Program name: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre Design, Technology and Production

description: The Minor in Theatre Design, Technology and Production provides students with a fundamental understanding of the visual and technical aspects of theatre. Students develop foundational skills in various areas of theatrical design and technology, including scenic, lighting, costume, and sound design, as well as stage management and related production technologies. This minor is designed to complement a wide range of majors, offering practical experience, fostering creativity, problem-solving abilities, and an appreciation for the collaborative processes inherent in live performance.
Program name: Minor in Theatre Design, Technology and Production

description: The Theatre Design, Technology and Production minor provides students with practical experience and training in scenery, costumes, lighting, sound, props, stage management, house management and/or technical direction related to live performance. Students in the minor may also learn about the broader industry, including scenic and costume rendering, production management and special effects.
Program name: Minor in Theatre Performance

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Theatre Studies is a liberal arts-based degree for students who want to develop a broad knowledge of theatre and hone their skills in performance, history, theory, dramatic literature, and other aspects of theatre arts. It is a flexible degree designed for students who want to become well-rounded theatre artists and professionals, to double major in another field, or to pursue graduate studies in theatre. The curriculum offers students the opportunity to choose areas of focus that align with their interests and career goals. Students choose three areas of focus from a list that includes acting, design, dramatic literature, playwriting, directing, stage management, and theatre history. Students are also encouraged to participate in performances, productions, and other activities within the School of Theatre and Dance and to take advantage of internship opportunities, both on and off campus.
Accreditation status: Accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD) and the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Theatre Studies

description: The Theatre Studies minor is designed to provide students with foundational knowledge of the history, literature, theory and practice of theatre. The minor provides a general overview of theatre studies that complements a variety of majors.
Program name: Minor in Theatre Studies

description: The World Music minor provides students with the opportunity to explore the various cultures, histories, and practices of music throughout the world. Through performance, analysis, and discussion, students will gain an understanding of the impact of music on cultures around the globe. Students will explore a wide array of musical traditions, including those of Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, and South America.
Program name: Minor in World Music
